question: to the Commission Stefan Köhler (PPE), Christian Doleschal (PPE), Norbert Lins (PPE), Alexandra Mehnert (PPE), Michael Gahler (PPE), Sabine Verheyen (PPE), Markus Ferber (PPE), Jens Gieseke (PPE), Angelika Niebler (PPE), David McAllister (PPE), Andrea Wechsler (PPE), Verena Mertens (PPE), Sven Simon (PPE) Subject:

Articles 12 and 15(8) of the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)1 introduce labelling requirements for reusable packaging, including secondary and tertiary packaging such as crates and pallets. However, their application creates a significant challenge for the implementation of the PPWR. Although Article 12 applies to packaging placed on the market after 12 February 2025, items placed before and after that date cannot be distinguished in automated systems. This may lead to a presumption of non-compliance under Article 15(8), effectively requiring retrofitting or withdrawal of large volumes of packaging currently in circulation. Retrofitting appears technologically and logistically unfeasible at scale, with potentially disproportionate costs. This risks penalising well-functioning reuse systems and undermining circular economy objectives. 1.
How does the Commission assess the feasibility of applying Articles 12 and 15(8) to existing secondary and tertiary reusable packaging?
How will the Commission address the inability to distinguish packaging placed on the market before and after 12 February 2025?

Will the Commission consider, in the relevant implementing acts, pragmatic solutions such as targeted derogations or transitional arrangements for existing packaging, where the core objectives of Article 12 are already met?

Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC (OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/40/oj).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.7.2026) Article 12 of the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation1 (PPWR) introduces harmonised labelling requirements for reusable packaging, including transport packaging. In its guidance document of 30 March 20262, Commission clarified, in point 14, that reusable transport packaging placed on the market before 11 February 2025 does not need to be withdrawn or retrofitted; if it was placed on the market after that date but before the application date of the new labelling requirements, it will have to be retrofitted only in 2032, after the expiry of all the transitional periods to comply with the new harmonised labels. Packaging in open loop reuse systems is exempted from the labelling requirements. The Commission recognises the practical challenges linked to identifying packaging placed on the market before and after 11 February 2025, in particular in automated logistics and reuse systems where packaging circulates for many years. The guidance therefore confirms that the PPWR allows for the provision of information via websites or accompanying documentation in the case of reusable transport packaging in business-to-business situations managed by a system operator in a closed-loop system. The Commission considers that the PPWR should support, and not disrupt, well-functioning reuse systems and circular business models. In preparing the implementing acts under Article 12, the Commission will therefore take account of proportionality, technical feasibility and the need to avoid unnecessary administrative or economic burdens. The Commission will continue engaging with stakeholders and Member States to ensure pragmatic and harmonised implementation solutions, including appropriate transitional approaches where justified.
1 Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging

and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC, OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025. 2 https://environment.ec.europa.eu/publications/guidance-document-packaging-and-packaging-waste-regulationppwr_en.
